story.title: Chinese court rules AI cost-cutting is not legal grounds to fire workers, setting landmark precedent
story.summary: A court in Hangzhou, China has ruled that a fintech company acted illegally when it dismissed a 35-year-old employee on the grounds that an AI replacement would be cheaper, rejecting the argument that cost savings from automation justify termination. The worker, surnamed Zhou, had overseen AI-generated responses and was offered a demotion and pay cut before being fired for refusing. The ruling is being watched closely as China grapples with rising anxiety about AI-driven unemployment, and the court affirmed that existing labour protections cover workers displaced by automation.
